synthesis.description: Each mid-year and year-end cycle, announced by HR with a schedule, managers ask staff to choose reviewers and list their accomplishments, staff send reviewer names and accomplishment bullets, reviewers write feedback, and managers hold a PRC meeting to rank people. Managers then write reviews on the PEP form, get signed copies back and communicate results, sometimes handling objections about who should review whom or how a rating was reached.
steps: HR announces the performance cycle and its schedule.
Managers ask staff to pick reviewers, entered in the PEP system or sent by email.
Staff submit their accomplishments and reviewers write feedback.
The manager schedules and holds the PRC meeting to rank staff.
The manager writes each review on the standard form and discusses it with the employee.
Signed copies are collected and filed.
synthesis.approach: Use a cycle checklist with fixed dates for reviewer selection, accomplishments, feedback, PRC and signed copies, plus a standard accomplishments form that asks for duties and results, so managers track who is outstanding in one view.
synthesis.rationale: The rounds repeat the same sequence and the stalls are late or misformatted submissions and a fallback when the system failed. A checklist with a standard form makes each stage and its owner clear; the writing and ranking remain people's work.
